Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Great Falls MT
625 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

 - Patchy to areas of fog persist through Saturday.

 - Another round of light to at times moderate snow develops this
   afternoon and persists through Saturday morning in northerly 
   upslope favored locations of North Central through Southwest 
   Montana.

 - Well below normal temperatures through Sunday, with
   temperatures slowly warming next work week.

&&

.UPDATE...

A cold core low moving southeastward over the Canadian Prairies 
will continue to send shortwaves and snow into the forecast area 
through Saturday morning. H500/H700 temperatures as low as 
-35C/-15C will ensure more efficient roadway accumulations tonight 
and wet surfaces from earlier melting has accelerated the process, 
with numerous travel difficulties/incidents being reported across 
central/north-central MT. 

The primary update for the early evening hours was to expand the 
winter weather advisory over the plains to include the I15 
corridor NW of Great Falls in addition to Chouteau County and the 
lower elevations of Judith Basin County. While snow amounts look 
to remain light in these areas, roadways were becoming slippery 
and icy with the loss of diurnal heating and visibilities were 
poor. 

Went with an 8 am expiration time, similar to the inherited 
advisories in light of the aforementioned colder shortwaves 
passing through during the overnight hours; however, the 
north/northwest section of this advisory may be lifted earlier 
than the 8 am expiration if the snow begins to shut off from the 
northwest prior to this time. So far the remainder of the forecast
looks on track, but conditions will be monitored of the remainder
of the evening. - RCG

&&

.DISCUSSION...
/Issued 444 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

Broad upper level troughing continues across the western US, with a 
reinforcing lobe of vorticity/compact upper low diving 
south/southeastward through AB and SK toward NE MT through Saturday 
morning. As the aforementioned upper system approaches this 
afternoon and evening, light to at times moderate snow begins to 
spread over much of the region. Ahead of the area of light to 
moderate widespread snow, there looks to be marginal, yet sufficient 
low-level instability to result in a few snow showers, mainly across 
Central and SW MT. The more widespread snow that develops through 
the afternoon and evening largely looks to be predominately light 
(snowfall rates of around 1/4" per hour); however, periods of 
moderate snow (snowfall rates between 1/2" to 3/4" per hour) are 
possible in northerly upslope favored areas. Given colder 
temperatures in place now, this lighter snow will have better 
success accumulating on roadways. This snow largely diminishes into 
Saturday morning, with areas in northwesterly favored areas seeing 
continued light snow through the afternoon Saturday. 

Transient ridging briefly builds in Sunday ahead of a much lower 
confidence forecast heading into next week. Several upper level 
disturbances off the west coast will be in place to open next week. 
Whether they move east across the Pacific NW or shift southward 
before moving east toward the Northern Rockies Monday remains to be 
seen. After the uncertainty to open the week, around 80% of cluster 
guidance members favor some form of at least weak upper level 
ridging and associated warmer than average temperatures mid-week 
toward Thanksgiving. - AM/Moldan

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Impactful Snow through Saturday Morning...

Confidence has increased that impactful snow will occur from the 
afternoon hours today through Saturday morning across portions of 
North Central through Southwest Montana; most notably in 
northerly upslope favored locations such as the Elkhorn and 
Boulder Mountains, Little Belt and Highwood Mountains, Upper 
Blackfoot and MacDonald Pass, Southern Rocky Mountain Front, East 
Glacier Park Region, Gates of the Mountains, Cascade County below 
5000ft, Northern High Plains, and Southern High Plains, Big Belt, 
Bridger and Castle Mountains, Gallatin and Madison County 
Mountains and Centennial Mountains, Gallatin Valley, and the 
Madison River Valley. For this reason a Winter Weather Advisory 
has been issued for the aforementioned locations through the late
morning hours on Saturday.

The table below lists the snowfall amounts for the low end (10th 
Percentile), most likely (50th Percentile), and high end (90th 
Percentile) scenarios within the NBM5.2 for select locations across 
North Central, Central and Southwest Montana from Friday morning 
through Sunday morning.

The low end scenario has a 90% chance that amounts will exceed the 
listed value or a 10% chance that amounts will be lower than what is 
listed while the high end scenario has a 90% chance that amounts 
will be lower than what is listed or a 10% chance that amounts will 
be higher than what is listed. The greater the spread between the 
low end and the high end scenario the greater the uncertainty is 
with regards to snowfall amounts, with a lower spread between low 
end and high end supporting a lower degree of uncertainty (higher 
confidence).

- Moldan

&&

.AVIATION...
21/00Z TAF Period

Scattered light snow will continue across the region through the
overnight hours with MVFR/IFR conditions expected and periods of
LIFR possible. Low clouds will linger around for a couple hours
following the end of precipitation before ceilings slowly lift
Saturday afternoon back to high-MVFR to low-VFR conditions.
Mountain obscuration will remain a concern through most of the
period.  -thor

Eastern Teton-Elkhorn and Boulder Mountains-Gates of the
